items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: in that band was Freight Marble as leader, and the rhythm section had a fellow named Slim on drum, they had Alvin Morgan on bass, and me on banjo

ctx.x: Okay, we're back to Willie Foster now.

Yeah, so I said I've taken Willie Foster's job on the boat, and in that band was Freight Marble as leader, and the rhythm section had a fellow named Slim on drum, they had Alvin Morgan on bass, and me on banjo, and the reed section was Willie Humper was in the reed section, had another fellow named Rylan, that's two, and another fellow named Mason, I believe it was Mason, he's a famous trumpet player out of St. Louis.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: I think that's when I went on the, on the boat with Faith Marvel.

ctx.x: Well, as I said, we, we, in Pensacola, we were working for these people, and so, uh, we used to play a town like, like Mobile, and go to Montgomery, and, uh, there's a couple other times we'd go. So, uh, around about, uh, let's see, close to 26, well, we left Pensacola, no, we made a trip down to Florida, that's what we made, a trip all over from Pensacola to, uh, Jacksonville, Florida. Well, this guy, here in the...

he was managing the band and booking the band because they didn't have no bookies no day, but he was a man that knew a lot of people, you see. And we booked this all the way to Jacksonville. We stayed, I remember it was in the winter we were in Jacksonville, Florida. And the fella George Morris, he had been a cook one time. He suggested that we go down to Miami or Panama, way down up in there, you see. And well, the fella, they wasn't doing so good on the road and everybody wanted to get back to Pensacola, you…
You missed out the, uh, the Lee Collins period there. Well, I, well, that, oh, yeah, that's right,

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: I worked with, I started with Fate Marble, and then they had a job with Sidney Desveen

ctx.x: And you were playing banjo at this time?

At that time I was born for the Stikker Steamboat Company. Uh-huh. And there was a ten piece band. It had three sax, three brass, and four rhythms. And you had to play banjo, you had to play pangeline guitar. If you were bass, you had to play bass following and bass horn. I worked with, I started with Fate Marble, and then they had a job with Sidney Desveen, and that's where he came to me. We used to play at the country club on Sundays. And that's where the Captain Vaughan came in and heard the band and I used to…
Yeah, for about ten years. And that's when you.
